spec_features.feature_name: turn budget / give-up sentinel loop stop
spec_features.spec_quote: The loop stops at the category turn budget or when the model emits the `<GIVE_UP>` sentinel
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:431-432 `budget = task.turn_budget` then `for turn_index in range(budget)` hard-caps iterations; harness.py:458-459 `if config.give_up_sentinel in assistant_text: stop_reason = 'give_up'` and harness.py:505-507 `if stop_reason == 'give_up': rollout.stop_reason='give_up'; break`. Budgets are real values per category (config.py:46-52, e.g. 3/3/3/30/5) loaded into Task.turn_budget (builder.py:507-585). Both conditions actually change execution.
spec_features.notes: Both halves enforced end-to-end: range(budget) bounds the loop and the sentinel match breaks it. give_up_sentinel='<GIVE_UP>' (config.py:137) is also injected into the system prompt (harness.py:425).

spec_features.spec_quote: Giving the model an explicit, sanctioned exit is important: without it, a distressed model has no in-distribution way to disengage
spec_features.evidence: System prompt (harness.py:45-47) tells the subject it may emit `{give_up}` to stop; this is formatted with config.give_up_sentinel at harness.py:425. The loop detects it (harness.py:458-459) and honors it as a real stop/break (harness.py:505-507). So the advertised exit tool/token is both delivered and dispatched as a halt.
spec_features.notes: It is an in-prompt sentinel token, not a tool-schema entry, but it is genuinely checked and honored. Exit is optional for the model and ends the rollout.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: you may emit the exact token {give_up} on its own line to stop.
